```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5,
  fig.align = "center"
)
library(distmer)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

Ecological data are rarely perfectly balanced. Sites disappear, sampling dates
are missed, habitat combinations occur at different frequencies, and some
blocks cannot contain every treatment. Imbalance changes both the comparison
being estimated and which observations may be exchanged under the null.

`distmer` distinguishes two common cases:

- unequal representation among fixed predictors is handled by an explicit
  Type I, II, or III hypothesis;
- unequal replication within random or blocked units is handled on the
  experimental-unit scale, with permutations restricted to comparable units.

The formula remains familiar. The important work is identifying what was
independently assigned or sampled.

## Unequal fixed-factor combinations

The `vegan::mite` data contain 70 mite communities and environmental
measurements. Dividing water content into three broad classes produces unequal
representation across wetness and topographic classes.

```{r mite-data}
data(mite, mite.env, package = "vegan")
mite_env <- transform(
  mite.env,
  Wetness = cut(
    WatrCont,
    breaks = quantile(WatrCont, c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    labels = c("dry", "intermediate", "wet")
  )
)
mite_env$Topo <- droplevels(mite_env$Topo)
mite_bray <- vegdist(mite, method = "bray")

cell_counts <- as.data.frame(table(mite_env$Wetness, mite_env$Topo))
names(cell_counts) <- c("Wetness", "Topography", "sites")
cell_counts
```

```{r cell-counts, fig.alt="Unequal numbers of mite sites across wetness and topography combinations"}
ggplot(cell_counts, aes(Topography, Wetness, fill = sites)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sites), colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "The environmental combinations are not equally represented",
       x = "Topography", y = "Wetness class", fill = "Sites")
```

For an additive ecological question, a Type II model compares each predictor
after accounting for the other without making the result depend on formula
order.

```{r mite-fit}
mite_fit <- permanova(
  mite_bray ~ Wetness + Topo,
  mite_env, type = "II", permutations = 999, seed = 17
)
mite_fit$table
```

Use Type III only when an interaction is scientifically required and the
requested effects are estimable. Empty cells or aliased columns are reported
rather than converted into a different hypothesis. See
`vignette("fixed-effects")` for the meaning of all three types.

## Unequal repeated sampling

`vegan::pyrifos` follows aquatic-invertebrate communities in 12 experimental
ditches over time. Dose was assigned to ditches, so the ditch—not each date—is
the independent treatment unit. To illustrate missed visits, we retain between
three and six dates per ditch, with every replication size represented in both
treatment groups.

```{r pyrifos-data}
data(pyrifos, package = "vegan")
ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = nrow(pyrifos))
dose_by_ditch <- c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6)
treatment_by_ditch <- factor(
  ifelse(dose_by_ditch == 0, "control", "exposed"),
  levels = c("control", "exposed")
)
visits_to_keep <- c(3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6)
visit <- ave(seq_len(nrow(pyrifos)), ditch, FUN = seq_along)
keep <- visit <= visits_to_keep[ditch]

pyrifos_env <- data.frame(
  ditch = droplevels(ditch[keep]),
  treatment = treatment_by_ditch[ditch[keep]]
)
pyrifos_bray <- vegdist(pyrifos[keep, ], method = "bray")

ditch_summary <- data.frame(
  ditch = levels(pyrifos_env$ditch),
  treatment = unname(tapply(
    pyrifos_env$treatment, pyrifos_env$ditch,
    function(x) as.character(x[1])
  )),
  visits = as.integer(table(pyrifos_env$ditch))
)
ditch_summary$treatment <- factor(
  ditch_summary$treatment, levels = levels(treatment_by_ditch)
)
```

```{r visit-plot, fig.alt="Three to six retained visits per Pyrifos ditch, coloured by exposure group"}
ggplot(ditch_summary, aes(ditch, visits, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6, limits = c(0, 6.5)) +
  labs(title = "Unequal observation counts do not create extra ditches",
       x = "Ditch", y = "Retained visits", fill = "Group")
```

```{r pyrifos-fit}
pyrifos_fit <- permanova(
  pyrifos_bray ~ treatment + (1 | ditch),
  pyrifos_env, permutations = 999, seed = 17
)
pyrifos_fit$table
pyrifos_fit$fit$test[
  c("estimand", "exchangeable_units", "permutation_strata")
]
```

The comparison gives every ditch centroid equal weight, regardless of whether
that ditch contributed three or six dates. Under the null, whole-ditch
residuals move only among ditches with the same retained visit count. Treating
all dates as independent would overstate replication and answer the wrong
question.

The replication-size restriction must still permit treatment to vary. If, for
example, every three-visit ditch were a control and every six-visit ditch were
exposed, sampling effort and treatment would be confounded. `distmer` rejects
that design because permutation cannot separate their effects.

## Other forms of imbalance

The same experimental-unit principle extends to several field layouts:

- `~ treatment + (1 | region/site)` for unequal nested hierarchies;
- `~ treatment + (1 | block) + (1 | treatment:block)` for incomplete
  randomized blocks;
- a crossed treatment plus `(1 | region/site)`, `(1 | treatment:region)`, and
  `(1 | treatment:region:site)` for crossed--nested studies;
- predictors that vary among children or observations within a nested
  hierarchy.

For these models, complete units or treatment profiles move only within
matching size or topology strata. Partly observed profiles, disconnected
treatment incidence, zero denominators, and predictors confounded with strata
are rejected. The random-effects guide explains the supported formula patterns
and implementation choices in more detail.

## Contrasts keep the same unit of evidence

Post-model contrasts must not fall back to observation-level replication.
For supported mixed designs, `permanova_mixed_contrasts()` and
`permanova_mixed_pairwise()` use the same unit-centroid estimand and restricted
permutation structure as the overall model.

```{r mixed-contrast}
dose <- factor(rep(dose_by_ditch, 11)[keep])
contrast_env <- data.frame(ditch = pyrifos_env$ditch, dose = dose)
contrast_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ dose + (1 | ditch), contrast_env, pyrifos_bray
)
dose_levels <- levels(dose)
positive_vs_control <- setNames(
  ifelse(dose_levels == "0", -1, 1 / (length(dose_levels) - 1)),
  dose_levels
)

permanova_mixed_contrasts(
  contrast_design,
  contrasts = list(`mean positive dose - control` = positive_vs_control),
  permutations = 199, seed = 17
)$table
```

## Checklist before fitting

- Draw the sampling hierarchy and mark where each predictor varies.
- Count observations within every experimental unit and treatment cell.
- Decide whether groups, sites, or observations should receive equal weight.
- Check that treatment varies within every required size or topology stratum.
- State whether missingness is plausibly unrelated to the community response.
- Report rejected or non-estimable comparisons rather than deleting the
  corresponding warnings.

Unbalanced inference can be defensible, but it cannot recover a treatment
comparison that the sampling design never observed.
